claims.claim: US telecom market is $451.7B (2025) growing at 5.88% CAGR to $601.2B by 2030, driven by 5G, AI data center connectivity, and $42.45B BEAD broadband stimulus

2025-2026 is the most active M&A period in US telecom history: VZ+FYBR ($20B), CHTR+Cox ($34.5B), TMUS+USCellular ($4.3B), SATS spectrum sales ($42.6B), LUMN mass markets to T ($5.75B), CCI fiber sale ($8.5B) — total deal value exceeding $110B

T-Mobile has overtaken Verizon as the largest US wireless carrier by market share (35% vs 34% vs AT&T 27%), with projected 40% share by 2026, driven by superior 5G network and aggressive subscriber growth (+495K postpaid phone in Q1 2025 alone)

US cable broadband is under siege from three fronts: fiber (99.7M homes passed, record), FWA (13.5M subscribers, +18%), and Starlink (2M+ US subs, 72% satellite ISP share). Cable lost 2.03M net subscribers in 2024 and 1.05M in 2025

Lumen Technologies has signed ~$13B in Private Connectivity Fabric deals for AI data center interconnection, validating AI-driven demand for dark fiber. Enterprise 'Grow' segment revenue +10.5% YoY, though legacy decline keeps overall revenue negative (-5.39% YoY)

Tower REITs show highest operating margins in the sector (AMT 45.5%, CCI 48.7%, SBAC 47.7%) but face headwinds from EchoStar's spectrum sale/network shutdown — Crown Castle most exposed with $3.5B+ in disputed DISH payments, triggering Barclays downgrade

EchoStar is executing a historic asset liquidation: selling $42.6B in spectrum to AT&T ($23B) and SpaceX ($19.6B), receiving SpaceX equity ~$8.5B. Transforms from debt-laden 5G builder to asset-light hybrid MVNO with Starlink direct-to-cell integration expected 2026

AT&T and Verizon (post-Frontier) both target 40-50M fiber passings, creating a national fiber duopoly. AT&T committed $250B over 5 years with $1.03B BEAD funding. Total industry fiber capex exceeds $30B annually

Charter's $34.5B Cox merger (FCC approved Feb 2026) creates nation's largest cable/broadband provider with ~38M subscribers, surpassing Comcast. Combined entity still faces structural broadband sub losses from fiber/FWA/satellite competition

Wireless-wireline convergence accelerating: T-Mobile entered fiber via $4.9B Metronet JV, Charter/Comcast partnered with T-Mobile for business MVNO, AT&T 42% fiber-wireless convergence rate. Pure-play operators face increasing competitive pressure

FCC under Chairman Carr eliminated 1,108 rules in 2025, advancing spectrum policy: AWS-3 auction 2026, Upper C-band (180 MHz) by 2027, 20,000+ MHz for satellite. BEAD $42.45B creates regulatory tailwinds for both wireless and broadband expansion

Revenue hierarchy: VZ ($138.2B) > T ($125.6B) > CMCSA ($123.7B) > TMUS ($88.3B) > CHTR ($54.8B). Top 4 = $476B combined. T-Mobile growth leader (+8.5% YoY), AT&T strongest profitability recovery ($22B net income, +25% YoY)
